name: Middle Fork Snoqualmie River
gaugeName: Middle Fork Snoqualmie River near Tanner
blurb: Clear mountain river under Mt. Si and Russian Butte, a half hour from Seattle.

sections.notes: Upper Middle whitewater. Wood and channels change; scout current conditions and identify both landings before launching. Bridgeview parking is limited. Concrete Bridge has a County hand-boat access just downstream of the bridge.

notices.title: Limited Bridgeview parking
notices.text: Use permitted roadside parking and confirm that the river-access trail is usable before setting your shuttle. The nearby trailhead is a separate facility.
notices.sourceName: American Whitewater — Middle Fork access projects

notices.title: Check road conditions
notices.text: Check current Forest Service road notices before driving the Middle Fork corridor; conditions can change with storms and snow.

putInAccess.sourceName: USFS — Middle Fork Snoqualmie management plan
putInAccess.note: The Forest Service describes existing Bridgeview road parking and river access. King County’s access plan locates the named site; its NAD27 coordinate is transformed to an approximate access-area marker. This is not the nearby trailhead parking pin or an exact landing.
putInAccess.directions: Use the Bridgeview river-access area along Middle Fork Road, a short distance downstream of the Middle Fork Trailhead footbridge. Parking is limited; use permitted roadside spaces and check current Forest Service road conditions.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: King County — Middle Fork Snoqualmie Natural Area
takeOutAccess.note: King County confirms kayak, raft and canoe access just below the bridge. Its access plan calls this Granite Creek and supplies the facility-area coordinate. The marker is approximate, not an exact landing or the separate Granite Creek hiking trailhead.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the public hand-boat access just downstream of the concrete bridge on SE Lake Dorothy Road. King County lists road-shoulder parking. Identify the usable river trail before launching or setting your shuttle.

sections.notes: Middle-Middle technical whitewater, including House Rocks. Experienced paddlers should check current wood and flows and scout as needed. Use the Concrete Bridge hand-boat access and the designated Tanner Road parking and public access trail.
sections.routeReview: Approximate Middle Fork Snoqualmie river-course overview only; not a safe line through rapids or a mapped connection to the shore.

notices.title: Tanner Road End takeout
notices.text: This stretch ends at the established access off SE Tanner Road. Tanner Landing Park is a different site farther downstream. Use designated parking and the public access trail.
notices.sourceName: King County — Middle Fork access plan

notices.title: Technical whitewater
notices.text: This is the Middle-Middle whitewater run. The dotted course shows general river bends; it does not identify safe rapid lines, current wood or usable shoreline landings.

putInAccess.sourceName: King County — Middle Fork Snoqualmie Natural Area
putInAccess.note: King County confirms kayak, raft and canoe access just below the bridge. Its access plan calls this Granite Creek and supplies the facility-area coordinate. The marker is approximate, not an exact landing or the separate Granite Creek hiking trailhead.
putInAccess.directions: Use the public hand-boat access just downstream of the concrete bridge on SE Lake Dorothy Road. King County lists road-shoulder parking. Identify the usable river trail before launching or setting your shuttle.

takeOutAccess.sourceName: King County — Middle Fork Snoqualmie access plan
takeOutAccess.note: The County plan documents the existing public boating access at Tanner Road End and gives its coordinate. American Whitewater’s current project history describes the designated parking retained during nearby housing development. Approximate access area only; no exact landing or route across neighboring property is mapped.
takeOutAccess.directions: Use the established river-access trail from SE Tanner Road and the designated roadside parking. Stay on the public access corridor and keep driveways clear. This takeout is Tanner Road End, upstream of Tanner Landing Park.

timing.note: A reviewed speed/flow calibration has not been established. Access and guide information remain available.

mapAuditNote: Three public access identities supported by County and USFS sources; county-plan coordinates are shown as approximate facility areas. Both sections have individually reviewed access maps. Upper course geometry remains withheld; no exact landing or bank-side claim.
